title: Everything sold off at once, and the Fed is talking about hiking
dek: A 10% week for the Nasdaq, gold down almost 10%, and US inflation back above 4% with December rate-rise bets near certainty.

mood.label: Risk-off
mood.explanation: The VIX closed Friday at 35.9, up about 86% in a week, and CNN's Fear & Greed index sank to 10, extreme fear, from 37 a week earlier.

regions.headline: Inflation at 4.1% turns the Fed hawkish as stocks correct
regions.summary: October CPI rose to 4.08% year on year and the Fed's minutes showed almost all officials expecting more rate rises, with some open to a bigger December move. Markets now price over 90% odds of a hike. The S&P 500 fell 8.6% on the week and the 30-year mortgage averaged 7.28% on 19 November, so borrowing costs are rising just as share prices fall.

regions.headline: Imported pain: euro stocks drop 7% on a quiet data week
regions.summary: There was little home-grown news, yet the Euro Stoxx 50 lost nearly 7% and the FTSE 100 5.1%. Euro area inflation was 4.01% in October with the ECB deposit rate at 2.5%, a wide gap to watch. UK CPI rose to 3.6%, though October borrowing came in below forecast, a small reprieve for the chancellor.

regions.headline: China misses across the board, Japan shrinks, India stands apart
regions.summary: China's October factory output, retail sales and investment all undershot forecasts, with retail growth down to 0.4%. Japan's economy contracted 0.1% in the third quarter while inflation rose to 2.3%, and economists now expect a Bank of Japan rise in December with the yen near 160. India is the outlier: inflation at 6.1% and rate rises expected, yet the Sensex gained 2.9% on the week.

body:
Normally when shares fall, something else rises. Not this week. The S&P 500 lost 8.6%, the Nasdaq 10%, gold and copper both fell almost 10%, and bitcoin dropped below $61,000. When every asset drops together, the usual cause is not a story about one of them but a change in the price of money itself — and that is what happened. American inflation has climbed back above 4%, the Fed is openly discussing another rate rise, and the AI trade that carried markets all year is unwinding at the same time.

## United States

Start with the number that moved everything. October CPI came in at 4.08% year on year, up from 4.02% in September, with core inflation at 2.87%. Minutes from the Fed's last meeting showed [almost all officials expecting further rate rises, some open to a larger December move](https://news.google.?oc=5), and markets now put [better than 90% odds on a hike next month](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMidkFVX3lxTFBNZ1RjcmN4eDV0ZlN1M1NLSmRIWG0yeWp3TGZsZmtlUldiX1RHei1ZUVN5dFBMLVFQeW0yMTV0MUlkNzFwMVUwOXhZWHgyWnNmUjVqOGZKS09lNWttakhCYmVxbDZVSTh2LU8yVVFFM25qdzA5WXc?oc=5). That is a world away from the cutting cycle investors were positioned for.

The cost shows up quickly in household budgets. The average 30-year mortgage was 7.28% on 19 November, up from 7.11% a week earlier, and the two-year Treasury yield was 4.76%. If you are a US business refinancing debt next year, the rate your bank starts from is going up, not down.

Against that, the real economy is merely cooling, not cracking. [Retail sales rose 0.2% in October](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxPc2k1UW1WejZUTnpFNU1INVhmLU43a2dmMEtrMlJJMk1Zdm8tSk4xd0hPMnJKTkJHcTlrb0dpMDJhQVgxLWNTT2tvMEdnWUZxZzFNSDh4NE11SzBuNmkzRHhMSzYyQ2M2NFNWZTY5TDhvdkVBSHZsMWpiemhMeWwxeC1VWlFOYWZCQnR2N1JnZ3h2a2N1LVFQbVgtc0hya3hKMzJKSFNNYzBTRWExOEE?oc=5), unemployment is 4.1% and GDP grew 2.07% in the year to the third quarter. So this is not a recession repricing. It is a valuation repricing, with [stocks sliding into a correction as AI worries intensified](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMif0FVX3lxTE5XYVdGdzl2am5CT1o3QlFFV2duR2dJZzNpbjlrYWg2cU4tVHJwZ0I4WWhaVmd3ZHQ0cTVyRklGcHprTlk0UFEzenE2T2ZNZ1pvNXdKbDBySkFDXzA5cktobkRxaTcxdkZzWGtfXzVzLXZqeEhnSDk5VEROWGRsNzQ?oc=5) and [copper's slide read by some as a growth warning](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxNOElkaGNZcUQ5TUdHaWZXWFFmSkxneEh4dE9oQks4aW9pWlJJUVNqQ0lUeVNNM1dhODVCeVgtMld4NF9pcGdUQWNsNHBVSGlMdWhoR0s1WFVheDlVMV93TWJMcVBHeks5TVhEMVlOQ0M4blUwd1czY3FZRHVralV2R0d0TWxvOHpa?oc=5). The 10-year yield actually fell on the week, to 4.91%. Money is leaving risk, not leaving America.

## Euro area

Europe imported this one. There was no great domestic shock, yet the DAX fell 7.3%, the Euro Stoxx 50 nearly 7% and the FTSE 100 5.1%. The euro slipped to $1.10 as the dollar firmed. The European Commission's new forecasts see [the bloc growing moderately, with France the weakest](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNc2k3bXJscXRZNnlPa3VxNTREb3djN2dXWVhFS1hwQ1ZFUkU0OF9KWnlLdFRPNHF1VEpVRGd2cmhJTGFDTnd4QTN4R0pmWmRtTkV2S1JuUTlBUTNCMzZxVDk0cEJWMzE5TjBVaVJwaFpJdzZ3TmRuWUNxeHpwSTJvbTZ4d0hQY284dmk0QWtLM0ZaQ0x0aHRZV1NxbHdaTzAxSTV3QmdsaExSTlJwb002RmZEYU93Qlk2?oc=5), and the ECB used its [November Financial Stability Review](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNM1k5cldKRUxEeDl2MmFyWk0xWVZ4ajFKUV90Si0ydVJTM1NtN3EzbF82dWM4Rjg0alF1Q3gwVjFMdm1keUtONkZDWHpQbzJ5TXp2WUJLS1AtZ3BjTzQ1UThYaUhFM1JWN2dpZC1IZEtkN1NTelJPek5vbVVkUXl5VHhMZnpWMWVWT1Jxb0lhMndvVXF2R1pCa3J0emRQMFBTTGI2WExBYzVBQQ?oc=5) to take stock of stretched asset prices — timing that looks sharper by the day.

The awkward arithmetic is inflation. Euro area HICP rose to 4.01% in October from 3.76%, while the ECB's deposit rate sits at 2.5%. In plain terms, savers are losing purchasing power and the central bank has far less room to soothe markets than its words suggest. In Britain, [CPI rose to 3.6%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxPNlJxR09ZamZkWXh4eEZLWUlacE5tcF9TQ2JZeE5rSDNvSWt5VjVGSnRkdUJOOGF6X3B3LTlGODRkaDNEM0pqOUZUXy15TWpfb0lkUHlWX3RnWHpveGtNdkZGMHBIRHNNVUV4YTE5VUp4T1RVT21xRDFPN1lpUUFlRWtkVm1Rak1lbl8tVEFvOVFUdW5pWnR3bnlFWk1KMi1IODQzWGNmYVJnWnhMRkVJWk1vcw?oc=5), another squeeze on real pay, though [October government borrowing came in below forecast](https://news.google.?oc=5) — helpful for a chancellor whose borrowing costs are set in the same global bond market that is repricing the Fed.

## Asia

China's October data was a triple miss: [factory output, retail sales and investment all undershot](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinAFBVV95cUxNVzZkMk1FbkdXMWpRaWFDbU05ZmJGY19kTS1BT2FjRE96eGRGSzNGY1l4cnAxS2VGVEY5SjE2a0E3S3h2TnhXV1RlbE1BYUVielk3ZEN3TTlaX0pfZ2M1VnVpNmp0bVZOczJ0cThYaFFLUUtyVXB4OUZjSDI5c3VHWVk3Yk80SzhVdlJxcVlwNS1QZG9TZ0dMVExLMm4?oc=5), with [retail sales growth limping to 0.4%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiUkFVX3lxTFBfZ0paUHJLMjhnamFzOUdfcDQ4c3puSnY5VTJQMjg1Y21FX09hYlZIdU5QZ1dKV0lpa1lkTGtSSGJ4QUttbXU2ZEpDNy13d2toUkE?oc=5) and [stimulus yet to show up](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitgFBVV95cUxPZjFiTE1FdTd4TV93WnROMERVZXMtQzdSZDRTOTh3cVhocV9Sb1NSRVVGelJYamtpWkwyLWc5WTc2MGRWVUJWckNkVVJTOVBUZTNuN3Jxdl92R1E3dWRySnk3RTAyZ3BlVVI2bGZKbjJKb0U4WkNSS1VJU3dQZ1B2eUJXaUF3TVZaWk4zS0N5RlVVSWRlcXZ4UkZQYl9nQkxrRkFxNF93dm94c0NLWEdCa1d3X2Z2UQ?oc=5). For European and American exporters, weak Chinese retail demand is the difference between a flat order book and a shrinking one, and it helps explain why copper fell almost 10% in a week.

Japan is caught between two pressures. The economy [shrank 0.1% in the third quarter](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxPTUwtR3JSMVMyTkNYeHRlQ3dxMDctN3pTQjdJMXdjRWlfNkt3ZkF4TmRXUEdQUmVtMHdqVzRvNjl3WVBiUF8yNjdxcWgwWHRxMDZBaDZrQU5qZ0l4RlJGOFJJS1l4N3RSbC0zaU5HY1N1VG41VWphZ29GemRSNjd1RDNfNGpSdjlmbzJFanNVcGZqTGdCTVZQRFNMTTZNMU5HT2dUYUdITQ?oc=5) as oil costs and soft spending bit, yet [inflation rose to 2.3%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxQS2lrVWd0VWlVS200R2doeXdmNUtXV0s4b2E5aldKeFlTem1UNGdud3lYR2JkeHdEUDk2LXR6SFk3LU83eU41dUh5VEdIWVBlYkx0ODMtZ2w4YU4zUl85Rmo4ZmszaDJIQVhpbE11LUItQkhJNFhTZHlCanpic0tpUDhZQzV3YV9tVjFlbg?oc=5) and [economists now expect the Bank of Japan to raise rates in December and again by March](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxNd2tVS3ktQThQZmhzbFBGVmwzRDlycmtudVhLTk1vLWpJeDlQMFBqV1J3bFZXNGtTT0VfRGJaWUxBeWNWck0tblgzbTJsQmM4SXNRbUVXZEo1Nk1UdWpONURjY1I5RnJsVmRuRzdra2VFSVlyYnJUTnhjUXNjNUJKU2YtWDBfQkZuWFV2d3FJZTdFSzZKdHgyM242QzVReUJENE52TEtXaWlfMnNlNGZkejlzRGR3TnM?oc=5). The yen is the reason: at about 160 to the dollar, every imported barrel and microchip costs more. India is the week's outlier, with the Sensex up 2.9% and nearly 15% in a month even as [inflation hit 6.1%](https://news.google.?oc=5) and [the RBI is expected to hike in December](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxPc0htMDdyM3NhYkRZMHFIU3V0VUhoNWs4ekl2elpzNWFnamZFZ0dXdnBseDNReXV6eklUTVZtUURSUlA2cWlRcFE5WXJMR3NDYUVsSkN6U2hRcGVyOW5GRzhmOWZvZG9IcjRxekRaYVk0MC1hdmVITnFMeE1QckpwSlpmS3daODhXREk5VDNxcGZ2bms0RFg1b2JPNmVxM09nWFhLWWczakZjSDBDS0VWTUNpcDBWc1E?oc=5).

## Debt and politics

Rising policy rates land hardest on borrowers who were already stretched. US federal debt stood at 121% of GDP in the second quarter and euro area government debt at 88.8%; France's 10-year yield averaged 4.89% in October against Germany's 3.42%, a gap that is itself a judgment on Paris. [Europe's welfare and defence bills are colliding with that arithmetic](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMigAFBVV95cUxPWGlkRXBMQWpFU3k3b3M3eFFWY0ZCZjd1cF9OMUZscWNlcnlyUzQ5aDJDd20taVZfTEF2ZXRSMmpjdXVfLUlSOVl1VGs4NjBSb1BORHU1eXEwdVFxMUItdnc0VzRiVkE1ZGZXVFhZR2Jrc09Sckc0a3hwdC1SSzVkbw?oc=5), and the ECB's top jobs are being carved up, with [France and Germany taking key roles and Spain lined up for the presidency](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxQemZrY1padmZ1Y2daZUJ5ajRIcDlZbklJekV5LUo5UWhWTEtwdGdHLWFCYThBU2ZBQmZaX0xRRmFLWkd3a1NVbjJBYzNFQXdna0YxMGZuMkU1TDRUa2VUODE5UWNqcm9udS1rUlJmRkFvLUxYb2JXZFpJZ0NsTmFISW5zRDdEWlZqSHJ2djk4U05GWGh6SHU1LVM2Ri1IcmoteVA5NWNmLVZHZnk5MFUzc01iR0dVaFhRREg5YkNTNHZZbUU?oc=5).

Geopolitics is adding to the bill. [Iran has kept up attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxNczJXN3dIbXJITGpRV1BQQzdMRlp4QVl0ZE5jZnM2Vk9SNm5tZ2ZJV1NlbXA4em01SGZxM3p3b0FQemFMS0dTNGhhdzdPZzhCdXZDVzJTRXYtRThDWHRQa3dZQzRTOGdPZWxuQThVTGo5RGVzUHluWnNVaWRmNE5XQ2VpSS1aMVZUT3IyOA?oc=5), [Poland says Russian missiles hit its territory](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxPS2NDX2gya2JxN0FLNlFBSjdJcXNqczVsWGJrNHdGVHoxNEF6a2hrSnlKc2hkVC0wSGROWkMzcXgyN0YtaHdMX0k0U043RE5BSkRXVGtlQ3h1Ym9iVk9uaVFnV0YyZEw0a3ZjRWxvUkZ6NHNGVWJSc1dDcEU5aUtrODZ5YTRQMVQ5UTA2WHd5U0ZGUkhybGllQXNseGR0ZHl4dC1JdGtPa2FGT3MzNzhXdkxrSU9XcENkLUE?oc=5), and a [Russian cargo ship was still burning off Finland](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxPTXUxa0FLT1o3Tzh4MUR0MV9ZenU1LU9PZl9QSzhsQXlOQThFNUxWbWFXRXZTOHFpb1lJdG1GTV9hOUZsc2x4YzBOSzV3ZHZkV2pyNjNIaTVWZEViQ2lLb3JkcjJsbGhVNXFmWXQ5c0pDTkVXeG9IbmlKV3AxYUtfNE5DVnhWX3lvNmg0SF9SZ1lHQzEtSnY1REsycUlvWFVEOFlBSXR3?oc=5) after an attack. Oil fell anyway — Brent down 6% on the week to about $90 — with [fears of a global supply surplus pulling against the Hormuz disruption](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixgFBVV95cUxOMnV0bXBXX1ZzNHpkcHFmanlPQ2FmczM3Z2xCcXRqRjYwTVB6SlFhZ29vbGcyM3V5a3lOMHZ3OXprMDM0ang4RVEwQmhFMTZ2QU1GT2lQN0ZPUXQyZWJ4MHR1S0JQTmE5Y0Z5dkZlemdFU0V6TWFId0pZZlFtbHVzaU1EeVl1S2RiSFdrcE95d1ZqQW9NRWlZUFNHWU9QVHNXRlZiTmEtckdWZEpScFREcVpPQ0x3MDNQeFhiZHJHMUlVQXFRNkE?oc=5). Cheaper fuel is the one piece of good news in an otherwise expensive week.

## AI and technology

The AI trade had two big moments this week, and neither lifted it. [Anthropic raised over $81bn in the largest offering on record](https://news.google.?oc=5), closed its first day [at a $1.3tn valuation](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxPeWZHVTllX0Nkbzk2Mkw2X2h1QXBNa213UlBfT3B6cXNsU2VvR3VMNWppZWRMMWFMb3RRcURkWG5rZWlpOERIY0prMk90YnVfaUkxWHRySUFkTG9sM0pHYVI1RHUwVkJnbkhDbmxha3FtYVRlcVloV1dDV194ZnRQZ3ROOWxSZw?oc=5), then [fell 13% the next day](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxOTnI5ZjRqcHhFQXkycDMySHZ1Tkl4V2RKdzNIcTlPdFhCMlJhZEkzX2RSZ0F0cjgteE9RX3JQejRRWHV6RnMtdXA3b3RKczRka0dxSEsyZU5SNFhUbTRZMU00NTVOdXE4RTI0OURfdE41aGIzc2N3ZnpsRFBxNkdsOUYzOGFnNEFGVkppNTVlTkR0OUstdU5jZWwyRUtOWGxVeEJBMWpiZ3FWRzVDdG8tUG1va3VWS2U0a3pWcg?oc=5) — and [Wall Street ended sharply lower as the debut failed to revive AI enthusiasm](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuwFBVV95cUxONFhTcEs0ZXJTOXhCWUVEQlBXR3BaeFdLVjdiNkNXdVFrNWtaVjFJRVc0cTcyRUJBRXBqV0JZUHUza3I0TndGYzZRX3N3eU4zR3plNl9wUkR5VU1FQ0phSjZEODlXYjJYQk5QaVRoTFotemhuTWFwSkhrYzFfNE1tM0JJNlBFY1BmNFNhS0FTeURyaGtHM2xJb3VoRE5LY0I1SVUxeko5dDJvRGlGam1ITllSRFU1OEV6T0tF?oc=5). Nvidia, meanwhile, is now [48% below its peak](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxQTGI3Sng2eVpHTHVCWFlFamhHRWxSYXNtMkU1R0Y1amNNMHRNMXdMQ0RNbHBNSXhvdlVIRU42Z0N4V3RWRGdzYnp6UjdkeDZsY2pwU29iRG9GR29NakVMV1FYRjdvWjdhckM1N0dmSVUwYjNXWU5yVVZQZm92U2tzNlpQMlNJZVRGTzNJbm1KLUpfUQ?oc=5), with [China's AI-linked shares shedding $1.7tn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxPRFM5M0lfajByTmNXWHhadkRCd19qQUJGU1FUM0ZUQnBXdVhDQU42NVF1X2RuUHJXUUt4QW41UWpnWS12aHNsX1JZU0RtSTBacFZTU0dncHpmOTRTLWJMbGRwY2pSeHFOTTI3dFFmcXJlRnQwcnRQSjlMSTh1a1pjdkRNQ1dCQlJlSGZPcXZQRk9MdUJBaWlUVFBzT2xCaUV2cUtQTXVCVVY0S0xDWFJEMQ?oc=5). Add [a nationwide FAA ground stop whose cause is still being investigated](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxPS1lDWmpyendldk0xZVAtZlFfeWlDLUpqN1pyZHVDMkhSZzdTNTBkOHBZcGZzVGhDTXY1VmpXeTRSaldQRlhFVGlWREU0WmUwV2VFTlpRbjFnWV9nTk9SZHJoelVNeXBBWThIWmI2VmkteTJWOUxzcmk3VVE0blJqc2QxOFdMWFVrZWoyS1BRdHFNMjNJWVJaRDNkUkQtQURXR2hteUF4NUJVMnl3ellFTlEtVmZyTjRxMXVHZjV3?oc=5) and the mood around technology has shifted from wonder to audit.

## Company news and results

Nvidia reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on 17 November: [revenue of $115.8bn, up 103% year on year](https://news.google.?oc=5), with [fourth-quarter guidance of $126bn to $134bn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihgFBVV95cUxOdVFCV0pER1Jmd2M2Z1NuaENSS3ZWN3hGeUZNZUk4S195SlhrMVdnaFpXc29TcDNCR2tJVXlMMDZZSVdzRnBPOFRYT0FBREx1U1h5STdoNmxBSHl2Um92azJ1MmtiRTBjWmRpaDVVcFdWblZOU2gxY2Nhc2xHWDNmbGx3MFNiZw?oc=5), above the quarter just reported, though the coming quarter includes an extra week. The company also said that [Jensen Huang will not return as chief executive](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxQOERUMkVEZEttRVd6TG92RVVFUzc4RU10anVtbFoxeV9RN1VneDJiUkc5NXpVWWNhM09PUWhGMHNHcmJNeTU0WTltdjA1TE5BbUtvOWx1QU4ySmJJc2lPWmoydVJld09sOER4Rk4xRE9QbXpKSVMzNE9ldENzQWZWVGZGRlY?oc=5); its results release names finance chief Colette Kress as interim chief executive.

Elsewhere, [Bayer agreed a Roundup settlement that could cost it billions](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxOWWlGNFE0V2hjbEJZVXZXMEhZRXZVbVlyeFNyWlRNQmtTUjAxNDdoM2ZITkN6elR0c043YlFaTjV6eGdSdk83VWswT1hUcmRlaWJHcVdwVWZDNGRUcmQzdWU1ZGtXeDhtM0M3MXFYMTNfR0swMWlvNVpEejBuSzJPcW5DaGU?oc=5), and the [EU and Indonesia signed a trade deal covering everything from palm oil to pharmaceuticals](https://news.google.?oc=5) — a reminder that while markets panic, trade plumbing keeps being rebuilt.

## Market mood

Risk-off, and not subtly. The VIX, which measures expected swings in the S&P 500, closed at 35.89 on Friday, up about 86% in a week and a level at which funds that target a set volatility usually have to cut their holdings. CNN's Fear & Greed index fell to 10 — extreme fear — from 37 a week ago. Credit spreads, the extra interest riskier companies pay to borrow, widened only modestly, to 3.52 percentage points, which suggests this is a repricing of equity hope rather than a credit event.

## What to watch next week

Thanksgiving thins out trading, which makes the two data points that do land matter more. US PCE inflation, the gauge the Fed actually targets, will either confirm the December hike that markets have already priced or force an uncomfortable rethink; after a week like this, there is not much cushion for a surprise. Monday's flash PMIs for the US and euro area give the first read on whether the market turmoil has reached company order books yet.
